title: Wiring of premises
summary: In short: this is the SA rulebook for low-voltage installs. The certificate of compliance hangs off it.
tip: On site: if a joint, gland, or protection choice feels clever, check the code before you close the board.

title: Small-scale embedded generation
summary: In short: extra wiring rules for a small generator that sits on a normal premises supply, PV included.
tip: On site: treat the PV install as part of the premises wiring, not a side project with its own habits.

title: Utility interface
summary: In short: how a small embedded generator is allowed to talk to the utility at the point of connection.
tip: On site: don't promise the client a grid-tie until the utility's application and this interface are actually sorted.

title: Simplified LV connection
summary: In short: a simpler path for small low-voltage generators, still the utility's call, not ours.
tip: On site: ask the municipality or Eskom which NRS path this site is on before you order the inverter.

title: PV commissioning pack
summary: In short: the inspection, test, and paperwork set for a grid-connected PV system.
tip: On site: fill the test sheets while you are still on the roof. Memory is a bad commissioning tool.

title: PV array design
summary: In short: how to design the array itself, not just hang modules and hope.
tip: On site: design the strings before you pull cable. Reworking a finished string is a rotten afternoon.

title: PV in the LV install
summary: In short: the low-voltage installation rules aimed at a solar supply.
tip: On site: the PV kit still has to live with the rest of the building's electrical install.

title: Industrial lithium cell safety
summary: In short: safety requirements for lithium cells and batteries used in industrial jobs, storage included.
tip: On site: ask for the cell standard on the datasheet. A pretty brochure is not a safety case.

title: Battery installation safety
summary: In short: the series that covers safe secondary-battery installations, layout and protection included.
tip: On site: ventilation, access, and isolation are part of the battery, not extras you add if there's time.

title: PV converter safety
summary: In short: safety of the power converters we use on PV, inverters included.
tip: On site: an inverter without a credible safety listing does not go on a client roof.

title: Anti-islanding tests
summary: In short: the test method that checks a PV inverter actually stops feeding an islanded grid.
tip: On site: don't disable anti-islanding to 'make it commission'. Linesmen are on the other end of that wire.

title: Anti-islanding
summary: In short: if the grid dies, our inverter must stop pushing power so the dead line stays dead.
tip: On site: prove it drops out when you open the grid side. A setting screen is not a test.

title: PLC languages
summary: In short: the common PLC languages. Structured Text in PC Worx and PLCnext lives here.
tip: On site: write ST the next tech can read at 10pm. Clever one-liners are how plants stay down.

title: Control system security
summary: In short: how to keep industrial controllers and networks from being an open door.
tip: On site: no default passwords, no surprise remote access, and don't hang the PLC on the guest Wi-Fi.

title: Field bus manners
summary: In short: a daisy-chained serial bus. It is not a star, and it is fussy about wiring.
tip: On site: chain it, terminate the two ends, and earth the shield in one place. Then label the A and B.

title: Modbus byte and word order
summary: In short: two boxes can read the same registers and still disagree which byte is the big one.
tip: On site: compare one known value, like a serial or a voltage you can meter, before you trust the map.

title: Scaling a register
summary: In short: the register is often a raw integer. The manual tells you how that becomes a real unit.
tip: On site: scale it in one function, then check it with a meter. Don't sprinkle magic multipliers through the ST.

title: PLC watchdog
summary: In short: a timer the program must keep kicking. If the code hangs, outputs should fall to a safe state.
tip: On site: decide what 'safe' is before you need it. A watchdog that does nothing is a comfort blanket.

title: Structured Text hygiene
summary: In short: names, one scaling spot, and a comment where the Modbus map isn't obvious.
tip: On site: if you can't explain the block in a sentence, split it. Future you is also on call.

title: Safe work and the CoC
summary: In short: you don't get to improvise with live gear. The CoC says the install meets the wiring code.
tip: On site: lock out, test dead, and don't sign a certificate for work you didn't actually inspect.

title: Registration, not a guess
summary: In short: some embedded generation needs a regulator or utility registration. The cutoff is not yours to invent.
tip: On site: ask which approval this size and this utility actually need before you energise in parallel.

title: Label the kit
summary: In short: if it isolates, feeds, or can shock someone, it needs a name the next person understands.
tip: On site: label polarity, string number, and what the isolator kills. 'DB 2' is not a label.

title: Isolate before you touch
summary: In short: open the right isolator, lock it, and prove the circuit is dead. Both DC and AC.
tip: On site: PV isolators on the roof and the inverter AC isolator are different switches. Open both.

title: DC isolation is not AC
summary: In short: DC does not pass through zero, so an AC breaker can weld shut trying to kill a string.
tip: On site: use the isolator that is actually rated for that DC circuit. Don't borrow one from the AC board.

title: Earthing and bonding
summary: In short: earthing gives fault current a way home. Bonding ties exposed metal together so it stays at the same potential.
tip: On site: a floating module frame or battery cabinet is not 'fine for now'. Bond it before you walk away.

title: String voltage on a cold morning
summary: In short: panels make a higher open-circuit voltage when they are cold than the sticker shows at standard test conditions.
tip: On site: size the string so a cold dawn still sits inside the inverter's max. A hot afternoon is the easy case.

title: String window
summary: In short: too many modules and the cold voltage is too high. Too few and a hot day may not even start the inverter.
tip: On site: do the cold and hot cases before you clip the string. Don't copy the last site's count.

title: Polarity
summary: In short: DC polarity swapped is not a small mistake. It cooks connectors and confuses the inverter.
tip: On site: meter every string before you plug it in. Red and black get swapped by tired hands.

title: Commissioning order
summary: In short: torque, polarity, insulation, voltages against what you designed, settings, then the signed sheets.
tip: On site: photograph labels and test readings before the covers go on. You will not be back tomorrow.

title: Torque the terminals
summary: In short: a terminal that feels tight can still be loose. Heat starts there.
tip: On site: use the driver and the value on the device, then mark the screw. Don't guess with a screwdriver.

title: Glands and UV
summary: In short: roof cable lives in sun and water. Indoor glands and unclipped tails don't last.
tip: On site: right gland, right cable, drip loop, and no bare DC pair flapping in the wind.

title: Where the batteries live
summary: In short: the room needs access, isolation, and a way for heat and gas to leave, matching the chemistry.
tip: On site: don't shove a cabinet into a sealed cupboard because it fitted. Read the install conditions.

title: SOC and SOH
summary: In short: state of charge is how full it is right now. State of health is how much capacity is left versus when it was new.
tip: On site: a battery at full charge can still be tired. Don't tell the client SOC and pretend it's SOH.

title: C-rate
summary: In short: how hard you push the battery compared with its capacity. Faster means hotter and usually a shorter life.
tip: On site: stay inside the charge and discharge rates the manufacturer published. Don't 'just try it'.

title: Listen to the BMS
summary: In short: the battery management system is the thing that stops a cell from being cooked or over-discharged.
tip: On site: if the BMS opens the contactors, find out why. Don't jumper it to finish the demo.

title: Generator plus storage
summary: In short: the genset, the grid, and the batteries must agree who is source and who is load.
tip: On site: interlock the sources. Two supplies on one bar without a break is how you wreck a alternator.

title: EMS modes
summary: In short: the energy manager is just a set of rules: what may run, from what, and when.
tip: On site: write the mode in plain language on the handover. 'Auto' is not a description.

title: Time-of-use arbitrage
summary: In short: buy or charge when energy is cheap, use the battery when it is expensive.
tip: On site: put the tariff seasons in the PLC where someone can see them. A wrong season quietly costs money.

title: Peak shaving
summary: In short: use the battery so the site does not set a new maximum demand. The demand charge remembers the peak.
tip: On site: agree the ceiling with the client, then alarm before you hit it. After the peak, the bill is already written.

title: Maximum demand
summary: In short: utilities often bill the highest demand in the period, not only the energy you used.
tip: On site: meter the demand the same way the utility does, or you will shave the wrong number.

title: Shedding load
summary: In short: when the supply is short, drop the loads you agreed, in the order you agreed.
tip: On site: label what is essential. Don't let the PLC guess that the cold room can wait.

title: CT direction
summary: In short: a current transformer backwards makes import look like export, and the EMS does the wrong thing.
tip: On site: check direction with a real load before you enable control. Arrows on the CT are there for a reason.

title: PV earth faults
summary: In short: a leaking string can sit there quietly and then bite when someone opens an isolator.
tip: On site: insulation-test the strings, and don't ignore an inverter earth-fault alarm to 'get through the day'.

title: DC arcs
summary: In short: a loose DC joint can arc and hold a flame. DC does not snuff itself every half cycle.
tip: On site: connectors clicked home, no half-mated plugs, and no homemade joints in a string.

title: How to kill it
summary: In short: everyone on site should know which handle makes the PV, the battery, and the AC actually dead.
tip: On site: walk the shutdown with the client once. A label on a door they can't find is not a procedure.

title: As-built, not memory
summary: In short: the drawing must match the strings, the addresses, and the breakers you actually left behind.
tip: On site: update the single-line before you leave. The next fault will not match last month's PDF.

title: IO and fail-safe
summary: In short: if a wire falls off, the plant should go to the safe state, not carry on at full chat.
tip: On site: pick normally-closed stops and alarms where a broken wire must be seen. Test that broken wire.

title: When Modbus goes quiet
summary: In short: a lost inverter or meter is not 'zero power'. It is missing data.
tip: On site: hold last good value only if you mean to, and alarm the timeout. Don't control on a frozen number.

title: Backup is not a UPS story
summary: In short: some inverters break, then make their own supply. Others only work while the grid is there.
tip: On site: tell the client which circuits actually stay on, and test those circuits with the grid open.

title: Access for firefighters
summary: In short: PV on a roof is still live in daylight even when the building main is off.
tip: On site: put the PV shutdown where the fire crew will actually see it, and label it in plain words.

title: Spare cores and addresses
summary: In short: leave a spare core and write the Modbus address on the device, not only in a laptop.
tip: On site: a sticker with the address and baud saves the next call-out from a treasure hunt.

title: Handover in human
summary: In short: the client needs what to do, what not to touch, and who to phone. Not a dump of manuals.
tip: On site: one page, plain language, plus the CoC and the test sheets. Then walk it once.
